premises.text: Rapid satellite growth creates spectrum noise that threatens consistent Earth–space communications
premises.evidence_span: As we go from 8,000 satellites to over 100,000 satellites in space, the issue that we're facing is that it's becoming much noisier

premises.text: Current obtain/coordinate/protect spectrum processes use ~25-year-old technology unfit for modern constellations
premises.evidence_span: using technology that's 25 years old for the legacy space industry rather than infrastructure for the modern space sector

premises.text: Spectrum simulations forecast co-linear interference events across satellite links
premises.evidence_span: We simulate how multiple satellites, when they will be in a co-linear event and potentially interfere with one another

premises.text: Coordination infrastructure automates operator workflows, ITU filing monitoring, and near-real-time protection of spectrum rights
premises.evidence_span: embed that simulation technology into coordination infrastructure in order to expedite the process of how satellite operators work together

premises.text: Platform serves as one-stop spectrum management and future spectrum exchange once interference is validated
premises.evidence_span: you can think of us as your one-stop shop for all spectrum management

premises.text: ITU community positioning aims to make the approach a new standard for operators and regulators
premises.evidence_span: We are moving forward for this to be the new standard for all satellite operators and regulators

value.text: Clear, consistent Earth–space communications through eased spectrum complexity
value.evidence_span: We need to establish clear communications on a regular basis

causal_links.evidence_span: without clear communications, the entire space sector becomes in jeopardy
easing the complexities of space spectrum
new standard for all satellite operators and regulators

notes: LOI/prepay/military contract counts excluded as traction. Demo uplink/downlink/intersat options folded into simulation mechanism (P3). Spectrum exchange kept with one-stop platform as roadmap of same commercial module (P5). Singleton D3 retained as independently revisable standards pathway.
